oil.when: 2008–2012 (Oil Life System reset with the INFO and reset buttons)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on with the engine off.
Press and hold the INFO button and the reset button together to open the personalization menu.
When OIL LIFE RESET shows, press and hold the reset button until ACKNOWLEDGED appears.
Turn the ignition off. The CHANGE OIL SOON message should be gone.
oil.note: Checked in the 2008 Getting to Know Your Malibu guide and the 2012 owner's manual. On 2012 cars the INFO and reset buttons are on the left side of the steering wheel.

oil.when: 2013 (MENU button on the turn signal lever and the thumbwheel)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition to ON/RUN with the engine off.
Press the MENU button on the turn signal lever to open the Vehicle Information menu.
Roll the thumbwheel until REMAINING OIL LIFE shows.
Press SET/CLR to set the oil life back to 100%, then turn the ignition off.

oil.when: 2016 (steering wheel controls on the right side)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Use the controls on the right side of the steering wheel to bring REMAINING OIL LIFE up on the instrument display.
Press and hold the check-mark (select) button for a few seconds until the reading goes back to 100% and the CHANGE ENGINE OIL SOON message clears.
Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the Tire and Loading Information label on the driver's door pillar (cold means parked at least three hours or driven under a mile).
There is no reset button. The low tire pressure light stays on until the pressure is corrected, then goes off on its own.
Acknowledging the CHECK TIRE PRESSURE message with the display buttons only hides it for now. It comes back at the next start if a tire is still low.
tpms.note: If the light comes on only on cold mornings and goes off as you drive, a tire is getting low: check and top up the pressures. If the tire pressure light flashes for about a minute when you start the car and then stays on, the warning system itself has a fault. A reset won't fix it; have it checked.
